data.title: Deutsche Bank got its dollar call for 2026 wrong. Why it's shifting tack now.
data.description:
By Jules Rimmer

Don't bet against the dollar yet; U.S. growth is stronger and its bond yields are higher.

The AI boom has been tremendously supportive of the dollar

Deutsche Bank was bearish on the dollar for 2026. It was the wrong call. The dollar index has risen 5.4% so far this year, not a huge move by historical standards but confounding many forecasts of the end of U.S. exceptionalism. Now, for 2027, Deutsche Bank has changed its view and predicts a "Superdollar," although "AI dollar" seems more appropriate.

The continuation of U.S. exceptionalism has forced Deutsche Bank's forex strategists Tim Baker, George Saravelos, Mallika Sachdeva and Charlie Hyams to revise their dollar DXY forecasts higher for 2027. These new targets are set out in a 2027 outlook piece dispatched to clients Thursday.

By the end of next year they predict the euro (EURUSD) at $1.15, the dollar to trade at 145 yen (USDJPY), for the British pound (GBPUSD) to be at $1.32 and for each Canadian dollar (CADUSD) to buy 0.83 U.S. greenbacks.

Those four currencies account for 90% of the DXY basket. The stronger yen is largely offset by a weaker euro.

Since its February low, the dollar has increased more than 7%. The AI boom, Baker writes, is largely responsible. It's pushed real rates higher, attracted huge equity inflows, exerted upward pressure on inflation and that in turn has turned the Fed more hawkish. "The AI dollar is alive and well," the report notes.

US economic outperformance is driven by robust capex spending

Baker and team now anticipate a "higher for longer" dollar in the first half of next year. This argument is supported by the U.S. topping the rankings for government bond yields and economic growth, as well as persistent equity inflows. This yield advantage is crucial in attracting international capital flows, especially from Asian countries recycling their immense trade surpluses.

The USD is hanging around high-yielder status - not an environment in which the dollar tends to fall

What might cause the weakening in the dollar that Deutsche Bank foresees in the second half of 2027? A slowdown in the AI boom, and a downgrading of capex expectations. That would lower bond yields and reduce equity inflows. Downside risks to energy prices from a potential resolution of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine could also contribute to dollar weakness. Further out, Baker and team worry about the large twin deficit the U.S. government operates.

Outside the U.S. Baker sees a difficult environment for the euro, especially given the political tribulations experienced in France, but he reckons much of the French risk premium is already priced in. Prospects for the euro should improve in the second half of the year.

In Asia, the report identifies plenty of scope for outperformance given those booming regional trade surpluses with the U.S. and their recycling into U.S. assets. Baker expects capital repatriation, Bank of Japan tightening and higher domestic yields to push the yen almost 10% higher in 2027.

-Jules Rimmer

data.title: FHLBank Chicago Invests $5.6 Million to Expand Housing Counseling Across Illinois and Wisconsin
data.description:
FHLBank Chicago Invests $5.6 Million to Expand Housing Counseling Across Illinois and Wisconsin

2026 investment builds on more than $13 million awarded since 2022 to expand housing counseling

The Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago (FHLBank Chicago) is providing $5.6 million in 2026 funding through its Community First® Housing Counseling Resource Program (HCRP) to expand access to housing counseling services across Illinois and Wisconsin. The 2026 funding supports the Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA) and the Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority (WHEDA), which work with networks of U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)-certified housing counseling agencies in their respective states.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119963953/en/

From left: Kristin Faust, Executive Director of the Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA); Katie Naftzger, Senior Vice President and Community Investment Officer at FHLBank Chicago; and Elmer Moore Jr., Executive Director and CEO of the Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority (WHEDA), celebrate FHLBank Chicago’s $5.6 million investment in its Community First® Housing Counseling Resource Program (HCRP).

“Housing counseling can be an important first step toward sustainable homeownership,” said Katie Naftzger, Senior Vice President and Community Investment Officer at FHLBank Chicago. “Through our partnerships with IHDA and WHEDA, we're helping more families prepare for homeownership while strengthening connections between housing counseling agencies and our member financial institutions.”

Launched in 2022, the HCRP expands access to financial education, credit preparation, and homebuyer support services. The program also supports current homeowners with post-purchase education and foreclosure prevention counseling. IHDA and WHEDA administer the program in their respective states, awarding grants to HUD-certified housing counseling agencies to expand their capacity to serve households.

Through the end of 2025, FHLBank Chicago has awarded more than $13 million through the HCRP, with participating housing counseling agencies serving more than 105,000 households across Illinois and Wisconsin. Nearly 9,000 of those households achieved homeownership.

“Homeownership is one of the most powerful tools for building equity and securing a long-term future, but for too many, it can feel increasingly out of reach,” said IHDA Executive Director Kristin Faust. “Through our partnership with FHLBank Chicago, we are helping first-time buyers overcome barriers to homeownership through housing counseling, financial literacy, and credit preparation. This direct support gives more families the guidance and resources they need to make informed decisions and build a strong foundation for sustainable homeownership.”

“Housing counseling agencies are essential to expanding homeownership opportunities across Wisconsin,” said Elmer Moore Jr., Executive Director and CEO of WHEDA. “Our continued partnership with FHLBank Chicago strengthens the capacity of these organizations to serve more households, expand their reach across the state and provide the resources families need to prepare for sustainable homeownership.”

The HCRP also strengthens connections between HUD-certified housing counseling agencies and FHLBank Chicago member financial institutions, helping connect mortgage-ready homebuyers with financing and other resources. These include FHLBank Chicago's Downpayment Plus® Program, which provides eligible homebuyers with down payment and closing cost assistance through participating members.

To learn more about the HCRP and view supported housing counseling agencies across Illinois and Wisconsin, visit the Housing Counseling Resource Program webpage.

About the Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago

FHLBank Chicago is a regional bank in the Federal Home Loan Bank System. FHLBanks are government-sponsored enterprises created by Congress to ensure access to low-cost funding for their member financial institutions, with a focus on providing solutions that support the housing and community development needs of members’ customers. FHLBank Chicago is a self-capitalizing cooperative, owned by its Illinois and Wisconsin members, including commercial banks, credit unions, insurance companies, savings institutions and community development financial institutions. To learn more about FHLBank Chicago, please visit fhlbc.com.

Community First® is a registered trademark of the Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago.

data.title: Merck and Isomorphic Labs Enter Strategic Research Collaboration
data.description:
Merck and Isomorphic Labs Enter Strategic Research Collaboration

Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, and Isomorphic Labs, an AI-first drug design and development company, today announced a research collaboration that brings together Isomorphic Labs’ AI approach to drug discovery with Merck’s rich proprietary data resources and deep discovery experience.

The companies will collaborate to discover therapeutic small molecule candidates against an oncology target of strategic importance. Isomorphic Labs will perform in silico predictions and deliver molecular designs, applying its proprietary drug design engine (IsoDDE) incorporating select high-quality proprietary data sets supplied by Merck for the purpose of this collaboration. Merck will be responsible for preclinical and clinical development, as well as manufacturing and commercialization of any products derived from the collaboration.

Under the terms of the agreement, Isomorphic Labs will receive an upfront payment from Merck and be eligible for payments based on the achievement of specified research, development, regulatory and commercial milestones, as well as tiered royalties on net sales. Isomorphic Labs also receives an option to co-fund development activities in return for elevated royalties.

“The key to successfully leveraging AI/ML for molecular invention lies in close coordination of wet-lab and dry-lab functions,” said George Addona, senior vice president and head of discovery, preclinical development and translational medicine, Merck Research Laboratories. “By combining Merck’s substantial internal data capabilities and discovery expertise with Isomorphic Labs’ powerful modeling and compute capabilities, we aim to identify new ways to design and create better candidates faster.”

“Through this collaboration with Merck, we will apply our world-leading drug design engine to unlock significant discovery progress,” said Sarah Skerratt, chief research officer, Isomorphic Labs. “By leveraging the generative and predictive power of the IsoDDE to address this challenging program, this collaboration highlights our companies’ shared commitment to innovation for the benefit of patient populations with unmet needs.”

The collaboration highlights the transformative power of bringing together advanced AI, unique data sets and established biopharmaceutical leadership to accelerate the advancement of therapeutic candidates, navigating complex biology with unprecedented speed and precision.

About Isomorphic Labs
Isomorphic Labs was founded in 2021, to transform drug discovery with the power of artificial intelligence, ushering in a new era of biomedical breakthroughs. Isomorphic Labs is led by CEO Sir Demis Hassabis and President Max Jaderberg. Isomorphic Labs has built a world-leading, modality-agnostic drug design engine (IsoDDE) comprised of foundational AI models. The computational drug-design system provides the predictive fidelity required to navigate novel biological systems with unprecedented accuracy.

The company is continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance drug design. Isomorphic Labs is headquartered in London and has office locations in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Lausanne, Switzerland. Isomorphic Labs is advancing a broad and ambitious drug design portfolio through partnered programs and wholly owned internal programs. For more information, go to www.isomorphiclabs.com.

About Merck
At Merck, known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, we are unified around our purpose: We use the power of leading-edge science to save and improve lives around the world. For more than 130 years, we have brought hope to humanity through the development of important medicines and vaccines. We aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company in the world – and today, we are at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions that advance the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals. We foster a diverse and inclusive global workforce and operate responsibly every day to enable a safe, sustainable and healthy future for all people and communities. For more information, visit www.merck.com and connect with us on X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and LinkedIn.

data.title: NIQ Appoints Danny Lange and Chris Tung to Board of Directors
data.description:
NIQ Appoints Danny Lange and Chris Tung to Board of Directors

Appointments add deep AI leadership and Greater China and Asia Pacific operating expertise to NIQ’s Board

NielsenIQ (NYSE: NIQ), a leading consumer intelligence company, today announced that Danny Lange and Chris Tung have been appointed to its Board of Directors, effective Nov. 18, 2026.

Lange brings more than three decades of technology leadership, including senior roles building and scaling artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities at Google, Unity, Uber, Amazon and Microsoft. Tung brings extensive operating, consumer and digital commerce experience across Greater China and Asia Pacific through leadership roles at Shangri-La Asia, Alibaba, PepsiCo, L’Oréal and other global businesses. Together, their experience strengthens the Board’s perspective as NIQ advances its AI strategy and expands its impact across global markets.

“Danny and Chris bring expertise that directly aligns with where NIQ is going,” said Jim Peck, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of NIQ. “Danny has spent his career building AI and machine learning capabilities at scale. Chris brings deep operating experience across Greater China and Asia Pacific, along with a proven track record of using data and technology to build brands and grow businesses. Their perspectives will be important as we execute our strategy, scale new AI offerings including NIQ Optiq and ConnectAI, and help clients grow in a rapidly changing market.”

About Danny Lange

Lange is the founder of Agentimus LLC, an AI advisory firm, where he advises private equity and growth equity investors and their portfolio companies on artificial intelligence. He previously served as Vice President of Business Intelligence and AI at Google, Senior Vice President of Artificial Intelligence at Unity Software, Head of Machine Learning at Uber, and General Manager of Amazon Machine Learning at Amazon. He also held engineering leadership positions at Microsoft. Lange serves on the boards of Trifork Group AG and ZeroNorth A/S. He holds a Master of Science degree and a Ph.D. in computer science from the Technical University of Denmark and is a named inventor on 24 U.S. patents.

“NIQ has a difficult-to-replicate AI advantage: trusted, proprietary AI-ready data grounded in real consumer behavior,” Lange said. “The opportunity now is to make that intelligence usable by the next generation of AI systems and agentic workflows, including agentic commerce. I’m excited to help NIQ turn that advantage into products and platforms that create meaningful value for clients and shareholders.”

About Chris Tung

Tung most recently served as Group Chief Marketing Officer and Chief Executive Officer, China, at Shangri-La Asia Limited. He previously served as President of Alibaba Group, leading strategic development, after serving as the company’s Chief Marketing Officer. Earlier in his career, he was Chief Executive Officer of VML China and held senior leadership roles at PepsiCo China, L’Oréal, GigaMedia and Procter & Gamble. Tung also created Alibaba’s “Uni Marketing” system, which used business intelligence to improve marketing and advertising effectiveness. His work has earned broad industry recognition; Forbes named him one of the World’s Most Influential CMOs in 2018, 2022 and 2023. He holds a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from Taiwan University and a master’s degree in industrial engineering from the University of Michigan.

“NIQ has a powerful global perspective on consumer behavior and a significant opportunity to deepen its impact across Asia and around the world,” Tung said. “As an NIQ client during my time at Alibaba, including when I built the Uni Marketing system, I saw firsthand how NIQ’s data can help brands understand consumers and make better decisions. I am pleased to join the Board and support the company as it advances its strategy and strengthens the value it delivers for clients.”

About NIQ

NielsenIQ (NYSE: NIQ) is a leading consumer intelligence company, delivering the most complete and trusted understanding of consumer buying behavior and revealing new pathways to growth. By combining an unmatched global data footprint and granular consumer and retail measurement with decades of AI modeling expertise, NIQ builds decision systems that help companies turn complex data into confident action.

With operations in more than 90 countries, NIQ covers approximately 82% of the world’s population and more than $7.4 trillion in global consumer spend. Through cloud-based platforms, advanced analytics and AI-driven insights, NIQ delivers The Full View™—helping brands and retailers understand what consumers buy, why they buy it, and what to do next.

For more information, please visit www.niq.com.

data.title: Alibaba's cloud business is thriving. But those profits are completely offset by losses from its AI labs.
data.description:
By Steve Goldstein

Alibaba's cloud profits are surging, but AI-labs losses are mounting.

The cloud-services business of Chinese internet giant Alibaba is thriving - but losses from its artificial-intelligence labs are completely offsetting it.

Alibaba said on Thursday that its fiscal second-quarter cloud and compute services adjusted earnings before interest, tax and amortization more than doubled, to 8.83 billion Chinese yuan ($1.32 billion). But losses from its AI labs business, which includes the Qwen large language model, tripled on the same metric to a 10.5 billion yuan loss due to heavy research and development and surging inference costs.

The company, which still makes most of its money from its core e-commerce businesses, said its adjusted earnings per American depository share jumped 86% to 8.10 yuan ($1.21) per share as revenue rose 10% to 271.52 billion yuan.

According to Visible Alpha, analysts expected earnings of 8.98 yuan a share on revenue of 269.42 billion yuan.

Alibaba shares (BABA) (HK:9988) drifted 1% lower in premarket trade, putting the stock on track for its worst close since Jan. 16, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Alibaba shares have slumped 43% this year.

Rival Tencent (HK:700) has seen its shares slump 42% in a difficult environment for Chinese tech stocks.

Alibaba's results show how difficult it is for AI labs to make money right now, even with surging demand. Anthropic, which starts trading on Thursday, posted a small operating loss in the third quarter after a small operating profit in the second quarter.

-Steve Goldstein

data.title: The stock market is being rocked by the biggest shake-up in a generation as tech falls behind
data.description:
By Joseph Adinolfi

Tech stocks are looking cheap, while defensive sectors like consumer staples are screening as expensive

The U.S. stock market has experienced a dramatic shake-up over the past couple of months.

Investors' sudden souring on the artificial-intelligence theme has coincided with a newfound fondness for shares of drugmakers and purveyors of consumer essentials like toothpaste and laundry detergent.

The shift has triggered one of the most dramatic stock-market shake-ups in decades. Not since the immediate aftermath of the dot-com bubble more than two decades ago have investors seen normally sleepy healthcare stocks outperform red-hot technology names by such a wide margin.

During the 100 days through Nov. 10, stocks in the S&P 500's healthcare sector XX:SP500.35 outperformed the index's information-technology names XX:SP500.45 by more than 33 percentage points, according to an analysis by Dow Jones Market Data.

That was the widest outperformance since October 2001. By then, the dot-com bubble had already burst, and major indexes were mired in a painful bear market made worse by the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks and a mild economic recession. As major indexes like the S&P 500 SPX and the Nasdaq Composite COMP struggled at the time, shares of Walmart (WMT) and other defensive stocks rallied.

As of Wednesday's close, healthcare was still outperforming tech by more than 22 percentage points - what would be its strongest relative performance since 2008, excluding earlier this year, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth, framed the shift as merely a reversal of what investors had witnessed during the first half of 2026, when shares of semiconductor stocks and other "AI suppliers" zoomed higher at a pace that drew comparisons to the final leg of the dot-com bubble in late 1999.

"After what we saw in semiconductors in May and June, it makes sense that the reversal would be just as powerful," Martin Adams said during a conversation with MarketWatch.

The recent changing of the guard could be a buying opportunity for investors who regret not being more heavily exposed to the AI theme. Nicholas Colas, co-founder of DataTrek, wrote in commentary shared with MarketWatch that other recent extremes in the relationship between tech and healthcare stocks have been followed by sharp reversals.

Risk is cheap. Safety isn't.

Tech's recent troubles have turned another longstanding relationship in markets on its head.

Based on forward price-to-earnings ratio - a popular valuation metric used by Wall Street analysts - consumer staples XX:SP500.30 and healthcare are both trading at a premium to tech. This represents "a big divergence" from the dominant trend of the past decade, DataTrek's Colas pointed out.

Put another way, information-technology companies are extremely cheap relative to their expected earnings growth, while defensive staples are expensive. Other metrics tell a similar story.

Short-term momentum gauges like relative strength indexes show that tech stocks are oversold while staples are overbought, said Michael Lebowitz, a portfolio manager at RIA Advisors, during a conversation with MarketWatch.

"Risk is cheap, but safety is expensive," Lebowitz told MarketWatch on Wednesday.

As of earlier this week, the S&P 500 information-technology sector was trading at 16.9 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, its lowest forward price-to-earnings ratio since March 2020. Consumer staples were trading at nearly 25 times, while healthcare was at 19 times. This is also "a big divergence" from the dominant trend of the past decade, Colas noted.

The big question for investors right now is whether or not this rotation is just the latest to emerge since the start of this AI-driven bull market. Investors saw something similar in the summer of 2024, and again during the fourth quarter of 2025.

HB Wealth's Martin Adams said the latest market action was giving her a feeling of déjà vu, as investors were discussing many of the same themes and potential pitfalls late last year, when nontech stocks were having an earlier moment in the spotlight.

Lebowitz used the examples of Walmart and Nvidia (NVDA) to illustrate his point. Walmart is now trading at a forward price-to-earnings ratio above 45, while Nvidia's is around 16.

"Nvidia doesn't need much growth to be a better buy than Walmart here," Lebowitz said. "Unless there's a lot more to this whole Nvidia thing than meets the eye. That's the risk."

-Joseph Adinolfi

data.title: Alibaba Earnings Rebound Sharply as AI Profitability Improves — Update
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Alibaba Group recorded a surge in fiscal second-quarter profit as its AI profitability and e-commerce business improved.

The Hangzhou-based company has doubled down on artificial intelligence as a growth driver, a push that faces a new risk from heightened scrutiny about exports of chips to China. It has committed to spending more than $53 billion over three years to develop both the hardware and software that power AI.

Its success on that front holds the key to staying competitive amid challenges from other big tech companies and startups alike. But going all in on AI has proved a drag on profitability over recent quarters, putting pressure on Alibaba to deliver on its AI goals.

Its latest results look reassuring.

Alibaba said net profit tripled from a year earlier to 64.535 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.68 billion, for the three months ended September. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected 23.72 billion yuan. Revenue grew about 10% to 271.52 billion yuan, also better than market estimates.

Alibaba said higher net investment income and income from operations drove the profit gains.

The earnings beat comes as the Chinese technology titan prepares a Hong Kong listing for its chip unit, T-Head, that investors view as a major validation of its efforts to produce in-house semiconductors. The business could fetch a valuation of $85 billion, according to Nomura estimates.

Alibaba on Thursday said its new AI chip, Zhenwu V900, is scheduled for commercial release for the first quarter of 2027.

But Alibaba still depends heavily on externally sourced chips, making it potentially vulnerable to tightened export controls. Its stock has fallen about 10% this week since the U.S. move to tighten export rules of advanced American-made chips.

The U.S. said this week that Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil will be added to a list of countries subject to export restrictions, a step intended to prevent Chinese customers from accessing data-center capacity in those countries remotely.

"We see this as a negative development for China's AI cloud industry, as tighter access to advanced computing resources could constrain AI model training and slow cloud revenue growth," Nomura analysts said in a research note.

Daiwa analyst John Choi said a rerating of China's internet sector is unlikely until investors gain conviction in Alibaba and Tencent, which will likely be the first stocks to be added if investors increase their China exposure. Concerns about Alibaba's elevated AI investment might ease if cloud profitability improves, he wrote in a note ahead of the results.

The company appears to be delivering on that front, with cloud business adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, and amortization more than doubling in the three months ended September, thanks to revenue growth and better operating efficiency. Meanwhile adjusted Ebita for its core e-commerce business more than tripled as losses in the food-delivery business narrowed.

Alibaba Cloud's recurring revenue from external customers rose 67%, driving faster overall cloud revenue growth, with profitability improving significantly, the company said.

Adjusted net profit--a metric closely watched by analysts, as it reflects core business operation profitability--rose 92% to 19.91 billion yuan. The measure excludes the effects of share-based compensation expenses, investment gains and losses, some impairments and other items.

"As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow," Chief Financial Officer Toby Xu said.

E-commerce business revenue rose 2% in the second quarter. Revenue from AI cloud and compute services jumped 53%, while AI labs and applications revenue climbed 51%.

Write to Tracy Qu at tracy.qu@wsj.com

(END) Dow Jones Newswires

data.title: Holland America Line Opens 2028 Alaska Cruisetours, Pairing Reimagined Oosterdam with Adventures Into the Great Land
data.description:
Holland America Line Opens 2028 Alaska Cruisetours, Pairing Reimagined Oosterdam with Adventures Into the Great Land

Holland America Line Opens 2028 Alaska Cruisetours, Pairing Reimagined Oosterdam with Adventures Into the Great Land

PR Newswire

SEATTLE, Nov. 19, 2026

Award-winning land-and-sea journeys take guests deeper into Alaska and Canada, from Denali National Park to the Yukon

SEATTLE, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bookings are open for Holland America Line's 2028 Alaska Cruisetour season, giving guests their first opportunity to pair an overland journey into the Great Land with a cruise aboard the reimagined Oosterdam. Following its Holland America Evolution transformation, Oosterdam will make its Alaska debut in 2028, bringing new onboard experiences to a Cruisetour program that combines the coast with deeper exploration into Alaska's interior.

 Holland America Line opens 2028 Alaska Cruisetours, pairing reimagined Oosterdam with journeys into Alaska's interior.

The 2028 season comes as Holland America Line celebrates two new awards distinguishing its place as a leader in Alaska vacations. U.S. News & World Report named Holland America the No. 1 Best Cruise Line in Alaska. U.S. News said Holland America earned the number one ranking this week because of "its extensive regional itineraries, decades of sailing experience, coveted Glacier Bay permits and 'Glacier Guarantee.'" And Holland America Line's 12-Day Signature Denali Cruisetour was named a winner in Good Housekeeping's Travel Awards. In its award summary, Good Housekeeping cited the ability to explore on land and sea, renovations to Holland America Denali Lodge and amazing glacier views.

Guests can choose from 19 Cruisetours itineraries aboard four ships, ranging from nine to 17 days operating between May and September. Each experience combines an Alaska cruise with an overland journey that includes a stay at the newly transformed Holland America Denali Lodge, following completion of its $70 million multi-year enhancement project in 2027. At the doorstep of Denali National Park & Preserve, the lodge will offer guests refreshed accommodations and public spaces, expanded dining experiences and other property enhancements. Each Cruisetour also includes a tour into the park and travel through Alaska's interior by rail and motorcoach.

"One of the things that makes Alaska so extraordinary is how different it looks from the water and from the interior—guests sail past glaciers and rugged coastlines, then journey inland to the mountains and wide-open landscapes of Denali National Park," said Dan Rough, vice president of revenue management for Holland America Line. "A Cruisetour brings everything together, and after generations of exploring Alaska, Holland America Line has the experience to help guests see more of the Great Land in one journey. We also are excited to add the reimagined Oosterdam to our Cruisetour lineup in 2028."

Classic, Signature and Ultimate Alaska & Denali Cruisetours pair the overland experience with a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise aboard Oosterdam or Eurodam, while Alaska, Denali & Yukon Cruisetours travel farther into Canada's Yukon Territory with either a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise or a shorter Alaska Inside Passage cruise aboard Koningsdam or Zaandam. Holland America Line is the only cruise line to take guests into the Yukon on a Cruisetour, traveling beyond Skagway to Whitehorse and Dawson City.

Experience Alaska from Ship to Interior
Highlights for 2028 include:

  • Holland America Evolution comes to Alaska: For the first time, guests can experience Holland America Evolution in Alaska aboard Oosterdam. The reimagined ship features purpose-built Solo Verandah staterooms, Bridgeview Suites with panoramic forward-facing views, Grand Dutch Café, refreshed accommodations and updated guest spaces, bringing the cruise line's largest fleet investment in its 153-year history to a destination where Holland America Line has long been a leader.
  • Holland America Denali Lodge at the doorstep of Denali National Park: Every Cruisetour includes a stay at Holland America Denali Lodge. Guests in 2028 will experience Holland America Denali Lodge following completion of its $70 million multi-year enhancement project, including two new guest buildings adding 72 rooms, refreshed public spaces and expanded dining experiences. Included tours take guests into Denali National Park & Preserve. Two- and three-night stays at Holland America Denali Lodge include the Tundra Wilderness Tour, while one-night stays include the Denali Natural History Tour.
  • Alaska by rail and motorcoach: Every Cruisetour includes travel aboard the glass-domed McKinley Explorer, with panoramic views, an open-air viewing platform, onboard commentary and dining. Holland America Line's owned railcars, motorcoaches and properties help connect each stage of the overland experience. Select itineraries also feature the historic White Pass & Yukon Route Railway and Direct-to-Denali service, taking guests from ship to Holland America Denali Lodge in a single day.
  • Alaska flavors and experiences ashore: At Holland America Denali Lodge, guests can experience destination programming at Denali Square, Music of Denali dinner theater and dining inspired by Alaska and the Pacific Northwest. Recent enhancements throughout Holland America Denali Lodge include expanded culinary offerings, updated menus and dining venues.
  • Go farther into the Yukon: Holland America Line is the only cruise line that takes guests into the heart of the Yukon on a Cruisetour, traveling beyond Skagway along the historic Klondike Gold Rush route to Whitehorse and Dawson City. In 2028, guests can explore Dawson City as the destination marks its 130th anniversary, with select itineraries including two nights at the Holland America Dawson City Inn, the Klondike Gold Tour and travel aboard the White Pass & Yukon Route Railway.

Four Ways to Experience Alaska by Land and Sea
The 2028 season offers four Cruisetour styles, giving guests options based on the length and type of overland experience: 

  • Classic Alaska & Denali Cruisetours: Three nine- to 10-day itineraries combine a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise with one night at Holland America Denali Lodge and the Denali Natural History Tour into Denali National Park & Preserve.
  • Signature Alaska & Denali Cruisetours: Six 10- to 12-day itineraries combine a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise with two or three nights at Holland America Denali Lodge and the Tundra Wilderness Tour into Denali National Park & Preserve.
  • Ultimate Alaska & Denali Cruisetours: Three 14-day itineraries combine a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise, two nights at Holland America Denali Lodge and an extended stay in Alyeska, Homer or Seward. Each features a dedicated Tour Director on land and an included visit to the Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center, along with additional included experiences depending on the itinerary, such as the Tundra Wilderness Tour, Riverboat Discovery and Gold Dredge 8.
  • Alaska, Denali & Yukon Cruisetours: Seven itineraries ranging from nine to 17 days offer a fully escorted overland experience, with a dedicated Tour Director accompanying guests throughout the land portion of the journey and providing local insight along the way. Each includes a stay at Holland America Denali Lodge, an included Denali National Park experience and exploration of the Yukon. Depending on the itinerary, guests pair their overland journey with either a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise aboard Oosterdam or Eurodam or a shorter Alaska Inside Passage cruise aboard Koningsdam or Zaandam.

Have It All Early Booking Bonus and Free Dining Package
For a limited time, guests who book 2028 Cruisetours with the Have It All Early Booking Bonus receive the Cruisetour Dining Package for the land portion of their journey, a $869-per-person value that extends more of the inclusive cruise experience ashore. The package includes select meals at Holland America properties during the overland journey, as well as lunch aboard the McKinley Explorer. Depending on the itinerary, guests can also enjoy dining associated with Music of Denali and the Tundra Wilderness Tour.

Additionally, the Have It All Early Booking Bonus includes shore excursion credit, specialty dining, an upgrade to Elite Beverage Package, an upgrade to Premium Wi-Fi, prepaid Crew Appreciation and the cruise line's Best Price Guarantee.

For more information about Holland America Line's shore excursions or to book a cruise, consult a travel advisor, call 1-877-SAIL HAL (877-724-5425) or visit hollandamerica.com.

Editor's Note: Photos are available at https://www.cruiseimagelibrary.com/c/gngqtdqq

Find Holland America Line on Facebook, Instagram and the Holland America Blog. You can also access all social media outlets via the home page at hollandamerica.com.

About Holland America Line
Holland America Line has been exploring the world for more than 150 years with expertly crafted itineraries, extraordinary service and genuine connections to the destinations. Offering a perfectly-sized ship experience, its fleet of 11 vessels visits nearly 400 ports in 114 countries around the world and has shared the thrill of Alaska for nearly 80 years — longer than any other cruise line. In 2029, Holland America Line will welcome a 12th ship to its fleet. Savour the Journey isn't just a tagline, it's a reinforcement that the cruise line provides experiences too good to hurry through, connecting travelers to the world and each other. Award-winning enrichment programming, entertainment and cuisine that brings each locale on board, including a revolutionary Global Fresh Fish Program, put Holland America Line at the forefront of premium cruising. Holland America Line is part of Carnival Corporation, the world's largest cruise company with a portfolio of cruise lines operating in over 800 ports & destinations worldwide. (NYSE: CCL).

data.title: Trustpoint Xposure Completes More Than 200 AI Visibility Audits Across Professional Services
data.description:
AMHERST, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Trustpoint Xposure, a New York-based public relations agency that uses its own proprietary AEO Certification Framework, which is not an independent industry standard, today announced it has completed more than 200 AI visibility audits for professionals and firms across professional services, including legal, medical, financial and technology sectors.

Each audit records how AI search platforms, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, describe a professional or firm when users ask about them. The audits note whether the subject appears, how accurately the platform describes them, and which sources it cites.

How a Trustpoint Xposure AI visibility audit works

A Trustpoint Xposure AI visibility audit is a documented check of how AI search platforms describe a business or professional. The audit uses a fixed set of questions that a prospective client might ask, runs them across four platforms and records the answers, the sources cited, and any competitors named instead. The same questions can be repeated later to show whether the description has changed.

What the audits found

In the company's internal analysis, 88% of the professionals audited were either absent from AI answers or described inaccurately. Of those, 54% were absent, and 34% were described inaccurately, while 12% were described correctly. The company also found inconsistent entity information, such as differing names, titles, or descriptions across profiles, in 64% of audits. The figures are based on internal analysis, have not been independently audited, and individual results may vary.

Why professionals are missing from AI search results

No AI platform publishes its exact selection rules, and no result can be guaranteed. Common reasons a professional is missing or misdescribed include inconsistent details across websites, limited independent editorial coverage, missing structured data such as schema markup, and no Google Knowledge Panel. An audit identifies which of these applies.

What can improve AI search visibility?

Trustpoint Xposure's Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) work focuses on consistent entity information across the web, credible editorial coverage, structured data such as Person and FAQPage schema, and a Google Knowledge Panel or Wikipedia entry where a subject is eligible. Google and Wikipedia's editors make those final decisions, so the company does not guarantee either outcome.

How businesses can check what AI says about them

Businesses can ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google the questions their customers ask, record the answers, and repeat the check monthly. AI answers can change from day to day, so trends are more reliable than any single result. Trustpoint Xposure offers a complimentary AI and Media Visibility Audit that follows this approach.

Professionals in regulated fields, including law and healthcare, should follow their licensing body's advertising and confidentiality rules when acting on audit findings.

About Trustpoint Xposure

Trustpoint Xposure is a New York-based public relations agency that provides Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), AI visibility audits, SEO, and digital public relations. Its AEO Certification Framework is the company's own proprietary standard and is not an independent third-party certification. More information is available at www.trustpointxposure.com.
